sections.name: body
sections.value:
**Performance: PASS WITH NOTES** at `6c831f4eb1f293446ecd81cb1ec506849034dc68`, round 1 under C33/C34. No new timer, poll or executable launch site. The added work is not zero, and launch volume is not guaranteed flat.

**Presence round:** the fifth check rides the existing 60-second watchdog. It reuses that round's seats/scopes and adds **one `PRAGMA user_version` plus one global pending-FYI aggregation**. The existing partial index is `(recipient, held_at_ms, id) WHERE state='pending'`; sender/origin exclusion is residual work, not a peer-only index. Let P be pending rows, B backlog recipients, S all registry seats and C standing stall claims: aggregation follows P, returned metadata follows B, standing-claim matching is O(C x B), and recipient matching O(B x S). Scope/parent matching adds work for newly due seats.

Each newly due seat reads and decodes **all its pending FYI bodies**, including local daemon notices before filtering them out, then attempts a claim. A winner sorts peer FYIs, builds a capped listing, stamps the claim and audits the result. These are additional store operations, each store helper with its schema guard; the display cap does not bound body hydration/sorting. Successful unchanged backlogs stay quiet; a newer FYI re-arms, and all-target delivery failures retry on a subsequent round, not a new fast loop.

There is **one normal send per due backlog per live PA target**, falling back to the prime, never waking the stalled seat. Each target retains the existing cold/session check, possible forced-wake audit, delivery/queue costs and model turn. Thus D due seats and T targets can cause D x T sends in a round. A PA-targeted notice also incurs the PA-line work below; the watchdog's single direct aggregation is not the whole round's cost when notices fire.

**Delivery-time additions:**

| Path | Added work |
|---|---|
| Live non-control arrival | One role PK lookup plus its schema PRAGMA, before routing/deduplication; not only successful PA deliveries |
| PA arrival / PA warm flush | Another global backlog aggregation plus guard; when another seat has pending peer FYIs, one full registry list plus guard, O(B x S) matching and synchronous repository file walks; fleet-filtered backlogs are sorted before showing five |
| FYI-carrying enqueue / warm-flush attempt | One full registry list plus guard, an O(S) state map with one size-board mutex lookup per seat, and cloning/refreshing the batch; this applies even to batches without a state notice |
| Typed hook claim | Fleet snapshot only when the batch actually contains a relevant local daemon state notice |

Registry snapshots include historical/tombstoned rows, not just live fleet members. A PA carrying FYIs can take **both** registry snapshots. Per round the size board adds an O(live-fleet) map replacement, but no new transcript/status read. The sender warning is per FYI submission: question scan, then lowercase allocation and up to 15 substring-marker searches; it remains advisory. Explicit `fyi-read --pending` reads/renders the full selected pile, with no background reader.

**P214-N001 / C34 follow-up:** the bounded notice/list does not establish a bound on global scans, synchronous filesystem work, full-registry snapshots or concurrent batch allocations. CI proves behavior, not large-store latency/rows visited. These are accepted source-priced costs, not a demonstrated normal-use cost breach. No speculative indexing/cache redesign is required by this verdict.

**Execution proof:** exact-head [CI 42744931063](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42744931063), Rust job `129594630973`, upload artifact **13731521048** pinned to this SHA: **2,376 executed passed**, zero failures/errors; six skips reported separately by nextest. Verified the store-backed once-per-backlog/new-FYI re-arm and F170 ride-along tests, five `fyi_watch` cases, fleet-line/guard cases and all six spawn guards. Node22 npm: **2,281 passed, six skipped**; Node24, Rust lint and final delivers succeed. Frozen worktree clean; GitHub head matches and is CLEAN.

**Before/after:** the author's PR-body 12:35 reading reports 16 registration ps/min and 167.8 machine launches/s on main `04c9e107`; it is not my measurement. My earlier same-build reading is output `1522fd90`: 16 registration ps/60s, CPU25.23%, RSS335 to131.67MiB, machine191.3/s, explicitly early post-bounce and unmatched. No new local build/test/probe or synthetic traffic. **A #214 after-deploy reading remains owed.** Existing launch adapters can be exercised more often by the new notices; unchanged `spawn_sites.rs` does not predict flat counters.
